causes.text: Intel announced a six-month delay to its 7-nm CPU manufacturing process due to yield problems, pushing the release of its next-generation chips to 2022 or later and causing its share price to drop from roughly $61 to around $50.

source_info.title: Intel 7nm CPU delay sees shares slump as it falls further behind AMD Ryzen

effects.text: AMD's stock price rose approximately 6.5% and closed at $63.44 as investors shifted capital from Intel to AMD following Intel's announcement of delays and share price slump.

source_info.title: Intel delay sees AMD shares surge as investors rotate to rivals

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Intel announced that manufacturing defects would delay its 7-nm CPUs until at least 2022, leading to a sharp decline in its share price.
Investors interpreted Intel's delay as evidence that AMD would gain a competitive edge in advanced processors and capture market share, prompting them to reallocate capital.
As a result, AMD's share price increased by about 6.5% on July 24 2020, closing above Intel for the first time.

rationale: The effect article notes that after Intel's announcement of a 7-nm delay, AMD's stock price improved roughly 6.5% and finished at $63.44, reflecting investors' belief that AMD would benefit from Intel's setback.
counterfactual_analysis: If Intel had not delayed its 7-nm chips, investors would not have rotated as aggressively into AMD, and AMD's stock likely would not have jumped 6.5%.

adversarial_confounders.text: Overall bullish sentiment in technology stocks unrelated to Intel's delay.
adversarial_confounders.impact: A general tech-market rally could have lifted AMD's share price regardless of Intel's problems, overstating the causal link.

adversarial_confounders.text: AMD's own product announcements or earnings guidance around the same date.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Positive news specific to AMD may have independently driven the stock higher.

details.commentary: Rivian's execution setbacks and financial strain underscored how dependent Amazon's electrification plans were on a single young supplier. As doubts grew about Rivian's ability to deliver at scale, investors reassessed the reliability and cost of Amazon's future last-mile fleet transition.
